item.title: Nigeria's Dangote oil refinery swings to net profit ahead of IPO
item.description: Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery, which is seeking to raise $1.6 billion in what would be Africa's biggest IPO, swung to a net profit in the first nine months of 2026 as revenue more than doubled, according to unaudited results released on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Chijioke Ohuocha, Macdonald Dzirutwe
item.content:encoded: Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery, which is [USN:L1N456052 TEXT:"seeking to raise"] $1.6 billion in what would be Africa's biggest IPO, swung to a net profit in the first nine months of 2026 as revenue more than doubled, according to unaudited results released on Tuesday. The company posted a net profit of $4.73 billion for January to September, compared with a $117.2 million loss a year earlier. The refinery has benefited from rising demand for its products amid supply disruptions linked to the Iran war, helping it sell jet fuel into Western Europe. "Our third-quarter performance demonstrates the successful transition from commissioning and ramp-up activities to sustainable commercial operations," Chief Executive Officer David Bird said in a statement. Revenue rose to $22.48 billion from $9.19 billion, while core earnings (EBITDA) jumped to $5.52 billion from $627.6 million, as higher crude processing rates, stronger refining margins and improved operations boosted profits. The 700,000-barrel-per-day refinery generated operating cash flow of $3.68 billion, up from $364.7 million a year earlier, and ended September with cash holdings of $6.69 billion. It also moved from a net debt position of $1.73 billion a year ago to net cash of $650.8 million. The application period for the initial public offering, initially due to close on October 13, [USN:L8N45Y14M TEXT:"has been extended"] by two weeks to October 27 amid strong investor demand. Built at a cost of about $20 billion on the outskirts of Lagos, the refinery has reshaped Nigeria's fuel market since it started operations in 2024. It aims to double refining capacity to 1.4 million bpd by 2029. The refinery has helped reduce Nigeria's reliance on imported petroleum products and has emerged as a major supplier of refined fuels to domestic and regional markets.

item.title: Rendimientos bonos del Tesoro EEUU a 10 años caen, retornos a dos años cambian de tendencia y suben
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a largo plazo bajaban el martes mientras los inversionistas seguían de cerca los mercados de bonos europeos.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a largo plazo bajaban el martes mientras los inversionistas seguían de cerca los mercados de bonos europeos. En tanto, los retornos a dos años cambiaron de tendencia y pasaron a terreno positivo antes de la publicación de datos clave sobre la inflación en Estados Unidos. Tras el cierre el lunes por feriado del mercado estadounidense de bonos, los rendimientos a 10 años alcanzaban el martes sus niveles más bajos desde el 2 de octubre, tras registrar la semana pasada su máximo en 24 años. En el extranjero, los rendimientos de los bonos de la zona del euro, especialmente los de mayor vencimiento, bajaban, ya que la liquidación de acciones tecnológicas en Asia llevó a algunos inversionistas a refugiarse en la deuda pública. "Una de las razones por las que el mercado estadounidense se mantenía más o menos estable era lo que está ocurriendo en Europa. Y parece que, en general, simplemente estamos siguiendo las tasas europeas", afirmó Tom di Galoma, director general de Mischler Financial. Los inversionistas estadounidenses esperaban el reporte del índice de precios al consumo de septiembre que se publicará el miércoles para conocer la evolución de la inflación, que se ha mantenido elevada debido a que la guerra en Oriente Medio ha impulsado el precio del petróleo. Sin embargo, los precios del crudo caían el martes, un día después de que el Brent alcanzara su máximo en casi un mes, mientras los operadores seguían de cerca los ataques contra Arabia Saudita y las perspectivas de un suministro adicional de gasóleo procedente de Rusia. A dos semanas de la reunión del 27 y 28 de octubre, los operadores apostaban a que la Fed mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios y deje su próxima subida para diciembre. La probabilidad implícita de un alza en octubre se situaba en 21,6%, mientras que las apuestas por un aumento de 25 puntos básicos en diciembre estaban en 68%, según FedWatch. El rendimiento de los bonos de referencia de Estados Unidos a 10 años caía 2,29 puntos básicos hasta el 5,221%, mientras que el del bono a 30 años cedía 3,19 puntos básicos, hasta el 5,5671%. El rendimiento de los bonos a 2 años , que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas de tasas de interés de la Fed, subía 1,91 puntos básicos hasta el 4,81%, tras cotizar antes en mínimos de 4,7574%. El diferencial entre los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a dos y 10 años , considerado un indicador de las expectativas económicas, se situaba en 40,9 puntos básicos positivos.

item.title: Brazil announces bill to forgive $2.5 billion in micro-entrepreneurs debt
item.description: Brazil announced on Tuesday it would send a bill to Congress aimed at forgiving micro-entrepreneurs' debt with the government, adding it seeks to tackle about 12.6 billion reais ($2.51 billion) in debt.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazil announced on Tuesday it would send a bill to Congress aimed at forgiving micro-entrepreneurs' debt with the government, adding it seeks to tackle about 12.6 billion reais ($2.51 billion) in debt. The government said in a statement it was also launching a program to purchase micro-entrepreneurs' debt with the private sector. Micro-entrepreneurs (MEIs) make up a simplified Brazilian business category created by the government to formalize self-employed workers, such as food delivery and rideshare drivers, and small business owners The government said debt forgiveness would reach some 3.6 million MEIs, while the purchase program would seek to buy about 6 billion reais in debt with discounts of at least 90% The measures aim at creating conditions for the expansion of the economic activities of MEIs, it added The announcement comes less than two weeks before the presidential election runoff, with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva [USN:L1N45U128 TEXT:"behind in polls"] against Senator Flavio Bolsonaro "No one wants to be a MEI their whole life, people want to grow; It is up to the government to provide the conditions," Lula said at a ceremony to announce the measures on Tuesday ($1 = 5.0103 reais)

item.title: Adani's Mumbai airport holds off on winter flight cuts after airline pushback
item.description: Adani's Mumbai airport will not alter any airline slots during the winter schedule, a spokesperson said on Tuesday, holding off on international flight cuts planned in the coming weeks after pushback from carriers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Adani's Mumbai airport will not alter any airline slots during the winter schedule, a spokesperson said on Tuesday, holding off on international flight cuts planned in the coming weeks [USN:L4N45Z0CY TEXT:"after pushback"] from carriers. The airport and airlines have been at odds over plans to temporarily cut international flights to make way for the partial demolition of an ageing terminal, Reuters earlier reported. Adani Airports' Director Jeet Adani and CEO Arun Bansal had met with the Airline Operators Committee of Mumbai, the spokesperson said, and assured airlines that historic slot allocations would be fully respected The spokesperson cited commitments from airlines to support the rebalancing of traffic starting from the summer schedule. The AOC did not immediately respond to a request for comment A joint working group will draw up an implementation plan over the next two weeks, and the two sides will meet again on October 28 Mumbai International Airport had proposed a 33% cut in international departure slots to make room at Terminal 2 for about 5 million passengers moving from Terminal 1, emails reviewed by Reuters showed The AOC said in an October 2 letter that the proposal was "not accepted"

item.title: Azerbaijan's governing party defends school uniform rules after hijab dispute
item.description: Azerbaijan defended on Tuesday its decision to introduce school uniform rules that have led to protests over restrictions on Islamic headscarves, and told close ally Turkey to stay out of its domestic affairs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Azerbaijan defended on Tuesday its decision to introduce school uniform rules that have led to protests over restrictions on Islamic headscarves, and told close ally Turkey to stay out of its domestic affairs. Azerbaijan, whose constitution separates religion from the state and guarantees freedom of religion, is a secular former Soviet republic with a predominantly Muslim population. The dispute threatens to strain relations between Azerbaijan and Turkey, and highlights the challenges Baku faces in enforcing secularism. The government introduced rules last month that prohibit school pupils from wearing clothing that departs from the official school uniform or is incompatible with the secular character of state education. The rules do not explicitly mention the hijab, but some protests broke out this week after reports that some pupils and teachers wearing Islamic headscarves were being denied entry to schools. The Interior Ministry said on Monday that 37 people had been detained for disrupting public order while opposing enforcement of the rules. The governing Yeni Azerbaijan Party (YAP) on Tuesday criticised an adviser to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and lawmakers from Turkey's ruling AK Party for speaking out against Azerbaijan's new rules. The adviser, Oktay Saral, wrote on X on Monday that it was "unacceptable" to deny the right to an education to Azerbaijani students who wear headscarves. "A headscarf is not an obstacle; it is a requirement of religious belief," he said. "We expect Azerbaijan to reverse this mistake as soon as possible." In a statement, YAP condemned Saral's comments as "populist and irresponsible" and said they risked harming relations between the close allies, adding that the new rules were based on equality, secularism and the rule of law. It said Turkey was also constitutionally secular and warned Ankara against using Azerbaijan's education policies for political purposes. The principle of "one nation, two states" — used to describe the countries' close ties — did not justify interference in each other's domestic affairs or the imposition of political and ideological views, YAP said. It also rejected criticism of Azerbaijan's close relations with Israel, saying they were based on international law and mutual interests.

item.title: Report: Pats RB TreVeyon Henderson out multiple weeks

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson will be sidelined multiple weeks with a high ankle sprain, ESPN reported on Tuesday. Henderson will not require surgery for the injury sustained in the first half of Sunday's 45-17 home victory against the Las Vegas Raiders, and he is regarded as a "quick healer," per the report. The Patriots (3-2) likely will lean more heavily on starter Rhamondre Stevenson for Sunday's AFC East clash with the New York Jets (2-3) in Foxborough, Mass. New England also has second-year running back Corey Kiner on the roster. Henderson gained 22 yards on four carries and had one catch for 16 yards before departing with the right ankle injury. He has 163 rushing yards and one touchdown in four games this season. A second-round pick out of Ohio State in 2025, Henderson has rushed for 1,074 yards and 10 touchdowns and caught 37 passes for 243 yards and one score in 21 career games (four starts). --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Gianni Infantino received undisclosed $1.7M World Cup payment
item.description: Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino received a previously undisclosed $1.72 million World Cup payment, according to FIFA and IRS documents obtained by ESPN.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino received a previously undisclosed $1.72 million World Cup payment, according to FIFA and IRS documents obtained by ESPN. According to the report published on Tuesday, the lack of transparency surrounding the compensation is a potential violation of FIFA statutes. Infantino received the compensation in 2024 from FWC2026, the official U.S.-based organization set up by FIFA to manage and operate the 2026 World Cup held this summer in North America, according to IRS records. The $1.72 million was in addition to Infantino's salary and benefits from FIFA for 2024, which amounted to about $4.9 million. The additional compensation was not disclosed in FIFA's annual report in 2024, per the report. According to FIFA's own statutes, "The individual compensation of the FIFA President, the members of the Council and the FIFA Secretary General shall be made public." A FIFA spokesperson told ESPN that the organization "strongly rejects any suggestion there has been a violation" of the statutes. "FIFA does not pay a second salary to the FIFA President and complies with all reporting requirements in relation to compensation," read a FIFA statement. "The FIFA President's annual compensation, as well as other contractual benefits, are decided by the independent Compensation Sub-Committee. "FIFA strongly rejects any claims that it has failed to disclose any financial information and has violated FIFA's Statutes. FIFA accounts are independently audited, and all declarations are in line with tax regulations in Switzerland, the United States and elsewhere. "FIFA is fully focused on the FIFA Council meeting on Thursday and looks forward to discussions with its members to further grow the game following the most successful FIFA World Cup in history." It is the latest controversy surrounding Infantino, 56, who has been in office since 2016. Earlier this year, he came under fire for a since-aborted plan to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup to private investors. --Field Level Media

item.title: Own goal keeps Kashima Antlers perfect in Asian Champions League
item.description: Kashima Antlers earned a 1-0 win over Vietnamese hosts Cong An Ha Noi thanks to a own goal on Tuesday to move top of the table in the eastern league phase of the Asian Champions League Elite.
item.dc:creator: Michael Church
item.content:encoded: Kashima Antlers earned a 1-0 win over Vietnamese hosts Cong An Ha Noi thanks to a own goal on Tuesday to move top of the table in the eastern league phase of the Asian Champions League Elite. Nguyen Adou Leygley Minh's own goal in the 61st minute kept the J-League champions perfect after Toru Oniki's side started their campaign by thrashing Newcastle Jets last month. Kashima lead compatriots Gamba Osaka, who also secured a second win in a row when Tomokazu Myojin's team came back from a goal behind to win 3-1 against Newcastle in Australia. Nikos Vergos gave the Jets a 32nd-minute lead with a heavily deflected strike from the edge of the area but Yusei Toshida's header eight minutes later levelled the scores. Deniz Hummet, who scored the winner when Gamba beat Saudi Arabia's Al-Nassr to claim last season's Asian Champions League Two title, hit the decisive second with 17 minutes remaining and Welton Felipe rounded out the win with a late third. Fabio Abreu's 79th minute header earned Beijing Guoan a 1-0 win over hosts Buriram United in Thailand as the Chinese Super League outfit also secured their second successive victory. Japan's Kyoto Sanga defeated Ratchaburi from Thailand 1-0 to pick up their first three points of the campaign through Temma Matsuda's 88th minute volley while Shanghai Port were held to a 1-1 draw by Daejeon Citizen. Prince Ampem had given hosts Shanghai a 49th-minute lead but Diogo Oliveira headed in from close range five minutes later to earn the South Korean side a share of the points. Marcos Guilherme scored twice as Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta'zim took advantage of Pohang Steelers midfielder Jeon Min-gwang's sending off just before the break to win 2-0. Guilherme put the visitors ahead four minutes after the restart before sealing the points for Xisco Munoz's side with his second a minute from time. The first eight finishers in the 16-team league phase in both east and west Asia will advance to the knockout rounds of the competition, with the tournament's quarter-finals, semi-finals and final to be played in Saudi Arabia next April.

item.title: Fitch warns bond yield surge is worsening debt outlook for developed economies
item.description: Rising government bond yields are making it much harder for major developed economies to stabilise debt burdens, with countries including France, the US and Britain facing growing fiscal challenges, credit rating agency Fitch said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rising government bond yields are making it much harder for major developed economies to stabilise debt burdens, with countries including France, the US and Britain facing growing fiscal challenges, credit rating agency Fitch said on Tuesday. In a report, Fitch said benchmark 10-year government bond yields in the world's 10 largest developed economies had risen by an average of 81 basis points so far this year. That would contribute to a nearly $4 trillion increase in overall developed-market government debt, taking it above $75 trillion, or $68.5 trillion across the top 10 economies. The median 10-year yield across the largest developed economies is now 161 bps above the average interest rate paid on outstanding debt, making it harder to reduce or even stabilise debt levels France faces one of the steepest challenges. It would need to cut its primary deficit to 0.4% of GDP from a projected 2.9% this year to stabilise its debt burden, while a rise in effective borrowing costs to current market yields would require a further fiscal adjustment of about 3.1% of GDP The US is expected to run the largest general government budget deficit this year, at 7.5% of GDP, or $2.4 trillion, followed by France (5.4%), the UK (4.8%) and Germany (3.7%) Deficits are expected to widen the most this year in Germany, by 1.1 percentage points, followed by the US and Canada, both by 0.7pp, and to narrow the most in Britain, by 0.4pp By 2030, debt-to-GDP ratios are forecast to rise most in France, by 12pp to 128%, followed by the US and Germany. Japan's ratio is expected to fall 11pp to 185%.

item.title: Russia detains Japanese journalist on suspicion of spying
item.description: Russia's Federal Security Service said it detained a Japanese journalist accused of gathering information on Russia's defence capabilities, news agencies reported on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's Federal Security Service said it detained a Japanese journalist accused of gathering information on Russia's defence capabilities, news agencies reported on Tuesday. FSB said the journalist for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper had been detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region before he planned to leave Russia, and was subsequently transferred to custody in Moscow, Interfax reported. Russian state TV showed a man lying on a floor and handcuffed by three masked men in black uniform. A voice behind the scene tells him he is suspected of spying. TV also showed him boarding a plane accompanied by two FSB servicemen, then in a cage on trial in a Moscow court, which authorised his custody for nearly two months. Russia regards Japan as an [USN:L8N3ZG0NU TEXT:""unfriendly" country"] as it has joined Western sanctions against Moscow over the war in Ukraine. Japan's embassy in Moscow did not answer phone calls out of business hours. Russia and Japan never signed a formal World War Two peace treaty, with the main obstacle being an unresolved territorial dispute over the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories. Russian President Vladimir Putin [USN:L8N44F0CG TEXT:"visited"] one of the disputed islands in August, causing an uproar in Japan. Tokyo has said it would continue implementing sanctions against Russia and supporting Ukraine. One of the most prominent cases of a foreign journalist arrested in Russia was the detention of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich in 2023. He was found guilty of espionage by a Russian court, sentenced to 16 years and then freed in an East-West prisoner swap in August 2024.

item.title: Boeing delivers 57 jets in September, highest monthly total for year
item.description: Boeing said on Tuesday that it delivered 57 jets in September, up from 51 in August and 55 a year earlier as it works to ramp up production of its best-selling 737 MAX narrow-body. It was the planemaker's highest monthly total so far this year.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole
item.content:encoded: Boeing (BA.N) said on Tuesday that it delivered 57 jets in September, up from 51 in August and 55 a year earlier as it works to ramp up production of its best-selling 737 MAX narrow-body. It was the planemaker's highest monthly total so far this year. Turkish Airlines' order for [USN:L6N45F0ZB TEXT:"100 737 MAX jets"] boosted Boeing's September total of new orders to 165. The US planemaker still trailed European rival Airbus' [USN:L1N45U0QJ TEXT:"72 deliveries"] in September, but Boeing far outsold its rival, which booked only 17 new orders from two customers last month. Boeing's September deliveries included 43 737 MAX jets, eight 787s, two 777 freighters and four 767s, including three for Boeing's defense unit for completion as KC-46 aerial refueling tankers. The higher deliveries come as Boeing works to consistently increase 737 MAX output to 47 jets a month, which has taken [USN:L6N45813N TEXT:"longer than expected"], Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said during an investor conference in September. Through September, Boeing has delivered 475 jets this year, up 8% from a year earlier. That includes 363 737 MAX jets, the most the MAX program has ever delivered in the first nine months of a year. In addition to Turkish Airlines' order, Boeing booked orders for 20 737 MAX jets for Lufthansa, six 737 MAX and five 787 jets for Biman Bangladesh Airlines, and eight 777-8 freighters and two 777 freighters for Ethiopian Airlines. Another six 737 MAX and 18 787 orders came from unidentified customers. Boeing ended September with an official backlog of 6,371 jets, up from 6,156 at the end of August.

item.title: Monedas bajan pese a retroceso global del dólar, en espera de datos cruciales de EEUU

item.dc:creator: Froilan Romero
item.content:encoded: La mayoría de las principales monedas de América Latina anotaban pérdidas el partes, a pesar de un retroceso del dólar en los mercados globales, mientras la atención de los mercados comienza a centrarse en datos de la economía de Estados Unidos, cruciales para evaluar los futuros movimientos de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal (Fed). * Para el miércoles se espera que se de a conocer el IPC de Estados Unidos de septiembre, previo al dato del índice de precios al productor y las ventas minoristas un día después, para concluir la semana con la intervención del presidente de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, en el FMI el viernes. * [USN:L6N45Z0PF TEXT:"El gobernador"] de la Reserva Federal Christopher Waller dijo el martes que el reciente aumento del rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense refleja un mayor crecimiento económico más que unas mayores expectativas de inflación, que siguen "bien ancladas". * Los operadores ven ahora solo un 17% de probabilidades de que la Fed suba las tasas este mes, mientras que la posibilidad de un alza en diciembre asciende al 87%, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde ante una canasta de seis importantes monedas, retrocedía alrededor de un 0,3%, en consonancia con el descenso de los precios del petróleo y luego que, en la víspera, la divisa estadounidense alcanzara un máximo de 18 meses. * En tanto, el Fondo Monetario Internacional recortó en la víspera sus previsiones de crecimiento para América Latina y el Caribe para 2026 y 2027, y dijo que la mayor parte de la región está recibiendo poco impulso del auge de la inteligencia artificial que ha ayudado a otras economías a absorber el choque energético de la guerra en Oriente Medio. * El peso mexicano cotizaba en 18,3810 por dólar, con una caída del 0,70%, reanudando una racha de pérdidas que había interrumpido en la víspera, mientras los inversionistas evaluaban señales sobre el las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, subía un 0,43%, a 67.034,18 unidades, impulsado principalmente por firmas del sector financiero, mientras Wall Street abría a la baja al inicio de la licitación mensual, una movida habitual debido a que tiene cerrada la posibilidad de financiamiento externo por los altos costos a pagar. * En tanto, el índice bursátil Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires subía un 0,9% y los bonos soberanos extrabursátiles promediaban una ganancia del 0,2%, junto a un riesgo país con algo más de oxígeno en los 589 puntos básicos. * El peso chileno , subía un ligero 0,04%, a 981,50/981,80 por dólar. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , avanzaba un 0,13%, a 11.057,54 unidades. * El peso colombiano ganaba un 0,28% a 3.180 unidades por dólar y en la bolsa el índice accionario COLCAP (.COLCAP) subía un 0,42% a 2.541,70 puntos. * La moneda peruana, el sol , se depreciaba un mínimo 0,03% a 3,4410/3,4420 unidades por dólar. item.title: Walmart to offer 250-plus free medications, including GLP-1s, to employees
item.description: Walmart on Tuesday introduced a plan to offer employees more than 250 medications, including GLP-1s, insulin and inhalers at no cost, as the retailer expands healthcare benefits for its workforce.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Walmart (WMT.O) on Tuesday introduced a plan to offer employees more than 250 medications, including GLP-1s, insulin and inhalers at no cost, as the retailer expands healthcare benefits for its workforce. Here are some details: The largest U.S. private employer, with about 1.6 million domestic workers, is in its annual enrollment season, which runs through Nov. 6. The plan covers treatment at providers such as Mayo Clinic for serious conditions including cancer, plus free GLP-1s for associates with type 2 diabetes. Surging healthcare expenses have been adding pressure on Americans who are already facing rising costs of living from inflation and oil prices. "We're adding even more ways to help you and your family live better through comprehensive and affordable healthcare and benefits," Chief People Officer Donna Morris said in a memo. Associates evaluated for or diagnosed with conditions, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease, will get no-cost specialist evaluations, the company said. Walmart, however, would raise starting health insurance premiums by $1.50 per biweekly pay period to $39.80, according to its website. The retailer already offers benefits including 20 no-cost therapy sessions annually and up to $20,000 for fertility, adoption or surrogacy services.

item.title: Governo Lula anuncia pacote com perdão de R$12,6 bi em dívidas tributárias de MEIs a 12 dias da eleição
item.description: O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva anunciou nesta terça-feira um pacote que inclui perdão integral de dívidas tributárias de 3,6 milhões de Microempreendedores Individuais (MEIs), compra de dívidas privadas desses trabalhadores pela União, repasse direto de recursos para investimento no negócio e dispensa de emissão de notas fiscais.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo Caram, Eduardo Simões
item.content:encoded: O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva anunciou nesta terça-feira um pacote que inclui perdão integral de dívidas tributárias de 3,6 milhões de Microempreendedores Individuais (MEIs), compra de dívidas privadas desses trabalhadores pela União, repasse direto de recursos para investimento no negócio e dispensa de emissão de notas fiscais. Em evento no Palácio do Planalto a 12 dias do segundo turno eleitoral, o ministro do Empreendedorismo, da Microempresa e da Empresa de Pequeno Porte, Paulo Pereira, afirmou que o projeto, se aprovado, vai perdoar R$12,6 bilhões em dívidas tributárias de MEIs. Em outra frente, o governo lançará um edital do programa Desenrola voltado especificamente aos MEIs com o objetivo de comprar R$6 bilhões em dívidas privadas desse público com instituições financeiras. O desconto mínimo exigido dos bancos para a compra do débito será de 90%. O governo ainda informou que estuda um incentivo de até R$5 bilhões para fomentar a atividade de MEIs. Segundo Pereira, o chamado Pix MEI repassará até R$5 mil por beneficiado. "A gente está anunciando o desenho de um programa de dinheiro direto na mão das empreendedoras e dos empreendedores. Não é crédito, não é empréstimo", disse o ministro. O Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento informou que o Pix MEI é uma medida em "estruturação", sem detalhar quando será feita a implementação. A pasta reforçou que o empreendedor não precisará devolver o dinheiro recebido. "O objetivo é permitir investimentos que ampliem a capacidade produtiva, como a compra de equipamentos para um salão de beleza, a melhoria de uma barraca de alimentos ou a aquisição de uma moto elétrica para entregas", disse a pasta. Em discurso no evento, Lula disse que o momento é difícil porque atos do governo em época de eleição geram barulho e ponderou que "nós temos ouvido é para ouvir barulho mesmo". "Se o barulho que vier a acontecer for o barulho por atendermos uma aspiração de vocês, é um barulho bom", disse. Pereira também reforçou a defesa por um aumento do teto de enquadramento do MEI. O governo apresentou em junho um projeto que eleva esse limite dos R$81 mil de faturamento anual vigentes hoje para R$110 mil em 2027 e R$140 mil em 2028. O texto, que permite que um MEI contrate até dois funcionários, ainda não foi a votação no Congresso Nacional. Ao apresentar a proposta em junho, o governo estimou que o impacto fiscal da medida seria de R$1,57 bilhão em 2027, R$3,15 bilhões em 2028 e R$3,38 bilhões em 2029. Em outra medida do pacote, um decreto presidencial vai reforçar a não-obrigatoriedade de emissão de nota fiscal por MEIs na venda de produtos e serviços para pessoas físicas. Também serão dispensados de emitir nota fiscal e criar CNPJ os nanoempreendedores, categoria com faturamento anual de até R$40,5 mil. "Estamos retribuindo o depósito de confiança que os MEIs colocaram no país", disse Lula. O presidente buscará, em 25 de outubro, sua reeleição em disputa em segundo turno com o candidato do PL, Flávio Bolsonaro, que [USN:L6N45R01C TEXT:"liderou"] por margem apertada o primeiro turno eleitoral no início deste mês. Pesquisa [USN:S8N44201U TEXT:"BTG/Nexus"] divulgada nesta terça-feira apontou 48% das intenções de voto para o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial contra 45% do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), cenário de empate técnico. O pacote anunciado nesta terça representa o primeiro grande anúncio de medidas após o primeiro turno das eleições e atinge um grupo relevante de pessoas, já que o Brasil tem hoje 17,6 milhões de microempreendedores. Antes do primeiro turno, o governo anunciou ao longo deste ano outras iniciativas com potencial apelo popular, como nova fase do programa Desenrola, reajuste do Bolsa Família, fim da chamada "taxa das blusinhas" e linhas de crédito para caminhões e ônibus e para trabalhadores de aplicativos de transporte ou de entrega. Também foram prorrogados e ampliados os subsídios a combustíveis, plano que o governo tem tratado como uma resposta à alta dos preços do petróleo diante da guerra no Oriente Médio, além de defender que o benefício é compensado pela arrecadação extra da União por conta da alta da commodity.

item.title: EU approves Kimberly-Clark's $40 billion Kenvue acquisition
item.description: The European Commission has approved Kimberly-Clark's $40 billion acquisition of Tylenol maker Kenvue after the maker of Kleenex tissues and Huggies diapers offered concessions to address EU antitrust concerns.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Commission has approved Kimberly-Clark's (KMB.O) $40 billion [USN:L1N4560JM TEXT:"acquisition"] of Tylenol maker Kenvue (KVUE.N) after the maker of Kleenex tissues and Huggies diapers [USN:L8N45A15Y TEXT:"offered concessions"] to address EU antitrust concerns. Kimberly-Clark offered to sell all its tampon and other feminine hygiene brands in the European Economic Area, the EU competition enforcer said in a statement. "The brands covered by the divestment are Kotex (including the Lidie sub-brand), Camelia and Record," the Commission said. The Commission had concerns that the transaction would reduce competition in the tampon market, particularly in the Czech Republic, Estonia and Slovakia, because it would result in the removal of an important supplier. Turkey-based Dilek Gida Uretim, a distributor of leading consumer good brands, agreed to buy the assets Kimberly-Clark has committed to sell, the Commission said, adding that it had approved that transaction, too. "Dilek is a suitable purchaser given that it has, among others, the financial resources to maintain and develop the divested business, as well as the expertise to operate it effectively," the Commission said.

item.title: Supreme Court to hear Trump's fight to shield DOGE records from disclosure
item.description: The US Supreme Court agreed on Tuesday to decide whether President Donald Trump's administration can avoid handing over records to a watchdog group about its Department of Government Efficiency, an initiative aimed at slashing agency budgets and workers spearheaded last year by his former adviser Elon Musk.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court agreed on Tuesday to decide whether President Donald Trump 's administration can avoid handing over records to a watchdog group about its Department of Government Efficiency, an initiative aimed at slashing agency budgets and workers spearheaded last year by his former adviser Elon Musk . The justices took up the administration's appeal of a federal judge's order for DOGE to respond to requests by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington for information about its operations. The court is expected to hear arguments in the case and issue a ruling by the end of June. Washington-based US District Judge Christopher Cooper in April 2025 ordered the disclosures, finding that DOGE [USN:L1N3PU02B TEXT:"likely"] is a government agency covered by the federal Freedom of Information Act, or FOIA. The US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit refused to halt the judge's order. "We will continue to pursue transparency for the American people, who deserve to know the details of the Trump administration's efforts to unilaterally remake the federal government," said Nikhel Sus, chief legal counsel for the watchdog group, called CREW. DOGE moved swiftly after Trump returned to office in January 2025 to carry out his effort to downsize and reshape the US government, making dramatic moves to slash the federal workforce, dismantle certain agencies and redirect work to the president's priorities. Trump officially established DOGE by executive order on his first day back in office, specifying an "18-month DOGE agenda." DOGE announced on July 4, 2025, in a social media post that its "formal mission" had come to an end. DOGE said it had slashed tens of billions of [USN:L2N3PN10O TEXT:"dollars"] in expenditures, but its claims were [USN:L6N3WX0YY TEXT:"difficult"] for outside financial experts to verify. Federal auditors found that some of DOGE's reported savings across contract, grant and lease terminations were incorrect, lacked supporting evidence or included terminations that were already underway when DOGE was established, according to a report by the Government Accountability Office. Last month, federal auditors probing the protection of sensitive information and data during DOGE's access to multiple federal agency systems reported that, due to limited information they were provided, "Congress and the public lack assurance that systems and data were protected." Musk, the world's richest person, has financially backed candidates from Trump's Republican Party and supported Trump himself in the 2024 US election. Musk led DOGE initially but left the role a few months later. He then had a falling out with Trump over the cost of the president's tax and spending bill that was later patched up. DOGE SECRECY CREW said its intention was to shed light on what it called DOGE's secretive structure and operations. It sued to obtain an array of records from DOGE through the FOIA statute, a law that allows the public to seek access to records produced by government agencies, over its role in the mass firings and cuts to federal programs. The Trump administration contends that DOGE was an advisory body to the president and, under Supreme Court precedent, exempt from FOIA. In response, CREW sought information to determine whether DOGE was subject to FOIA because it wielded the kind of authority of an agency independent of the president. Cooper ruled that DOGE must turn over some records sought by CREW and that the group was entitled to question DOGE official Amy Gleason at a deposition. The Supreme Court in June 2025 granted an emergency request by Trump's administration, [USN:S0N3RG05M TEXT:"ordering"] the DC Circuit to narrow the judge's directives concerning DOGE. CREW then abandoned some of its information requests, and the DC Circuit in July of this year refused the administration's request to halt the disclosure — prompting the appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Prince William stops traffic outside Buckingham Palace for a game of cricket
item.description: Britain's Prince William turned one of London's most famous thoroughfares, The Mall leading to Buckingham Palace, into a temporary cricket pitch on Tuesday, where he was joined by some of the game's biggest names to promote his Earthshot climate prize.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's Prince William turned one of London's most famous thoroughfares, The Mall leading to Buckingham Palace, into a temporary cricket pitch on Tuesday, where he was joined by some of the game's biggest names to promote his Earthshot climate prize. The wide red-paved promenade in the heart of the city is more often seen as the setting for grand royal processions and patriotic flag-waving celebrations. But on Tuesday, William picked up a cricket bat for an informal game with current and former international players including ex-Indian captain Sourav Ganguly, West Indies legend Brian Lara and England captain Joe Root. Against the palatial backdrop, William - dressed in a shirt and sweater - clubbed away a series of gentle deliveries from Ganguly and posed for selfies with onlookers. "He batted alright," said Ganguly when asked for his verdict on the prince's skills. The event was designed to celebrate the ties between Britain and India - two passionate cricketing nations - as India prepares to host the annual summit and awards ceremony of William's Earthshot Prize next month. The prize, founded in 2020, honours five winners with £1 million ($1.32 million) each to scale solutions aimed at repairing the planet. ($1 = 0.7551 pounds)

item.title: US grocer Albertsons pulls annual outlook, accelerates turnaround efforts
item.description: Albertsons withdrew its fiscal 2026 forecasts on Tuesday and launched a review of its business aimed at cutting costs, lowering prices and reversing sluggish sales.
item.dc:creator: Sanskriti Shekhar
item.content:encoded: Albertsons (ACI.N) withdrew its fiscal 2026 forecasts on Tuesday and launched a review of its business aimed at cutting costs, lowering prices and reversing sluggish sales. The US grocer has battled cautious consumer spending, particularly by lower-income shoppers, as food and fuel costs climb, alongside market share loss to mass retailers such as Walmart (WMT.O) , discount chains and private-label brands. The review builds on a restructuring, announced in July, and is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter ending February 2027. By then, Albertsons also aims to provide fresh short- and long-term financial targets alongside a "comprehensive turnaround plan". "We must turn things around," Meg Whitman, the former eBay and Hewlett-Packard CEO who was named executive chair last month in a newly created role to help the grocer "sharpen its strategy and strengthen execution", said on a post-earnings call. The company needs to move faster to cut costs and reinvest much of those savings to lower prices and improve store experience, she said. CEO Susan Morris said Albertsons had accumulated too many initiatives, processes and layers of complexity over time, slowing the organization and increasing costs. "We're not satisfied with the results and the current trajectory of our business," she said. The expanded turnaround effort comes nearly two years after Albertsons' proposed $24.6 billion merger with Kroger (KR.N) collapsed after a federal court [USN:S0N3MD055 TEXT:"blocked"] the deal on antitrust grounds. Albertsons subsequently terminated the agreement. The company's shares rose 2% on Tuesday, reversing premarket losses. They had fallen 27% so far this year. "They have hard time remaining competitive on price as some mass merchants such as Walmart have used grocery as a traffic driver and have other high margin categories such as fashion to offset food's low margins," said Bruce Winder, an independent retail consultant. In July, Albertsons [USN:L4N43P1CZ TEXT:"outlined plans"] to expand private-label offerings and improve e-commerce, while restructuring its 11 divisions into four regions and centralizing merchandising. Albertsons on Tuesday described those changes as the first step in its broader turnaround. "We'll exit areas that are underperforming," Morris said on Tuesday. Albertsons in July forecast fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings per share in the range of $1.75 to $1.85 and projected annual identical sales to decline in the range of 0.5% to 1.5% after trimming its annual target. The grocer on Tuesday reported that its same-store sales in the second quarter ended September 12 fell 0.8%. But adjusted profit of 36 cents per share beat estimate of 33 cents, according to data compiled by LSEG.

item.title: Argentina seeks tribunal order against UK oil activity near Falklands
item.description: Argentina's government said on Tuesday it had filed a request for provisional measures with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea seeking to halt British-authorized hydrocarbon activity near the Falkland Islands.
item.dc:creator: Aida Pelaez-fernandez
item.content:encoded: Argentina's government said on Tuesday it had filed a request for provisional measures with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea seeking to halt British-authorized hydrocarbon activity near the Falkland Islands. The request aims to prevent the United Kingdom from exploiting hydrocarbon resources on the continental shelf of the Northern Falklands Basin, the government added in a statement. The filing "seeks to preserve Argentina's sovereign rights over its continental shelf and prevent activities authorized unilaterally and illegally by the United Kingdom," the government added. Addressing Britain's parliament after Argentina's move, Uma Kumaran, parliamentary under-secretary for the foreign office, said that "legitimate commercial activity in the Falkland Islands remains lawful, and the British government stands behind those engaged in it." Kumaran added that the UK would engage with the tribunal process but would not provide a running commentary on the proceedings. "The notification does not constitute a judgment by an international court or tribunal. It does not invalidate licenses issued by the Falkland Islands government, alter the islands' regulatory authority, or require lawful hydrocarbon development activities to cease," Kumaran said. Britain also announced it was taking legal measures to protect businesses from pressure to comply with Argentine domestic measures. Tensions between Argentina and the UK over the [USN:L1N4590CV TEXT:"territory"] that is controlled by Britain but claimed by the South American country have escalated. Last month Milei's government [USN:L1N4590D5 TEXT:"presented legislation"] to crack down on companies drilling for oil off the Islands. The government's proposal would toughen penalties on companies and individuals who participate in activities linked to natural resources in the Falklands, and in Argentina's maritime spaces without authorization from Argentine authorities. The new bill, which has yet to be approved by Congress, aims to revamp 2011 legislation with a tougher framework. Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said on X that the latest request aims to prevent the start or continuation of hydrocarbon development on the Sea Lion project. Oil companies Navitas Petroleum (NVPTp.TA) and Rockhopper Exploration, owners of the Sea Lion offshore project north of the Falklands, have previously indicated they do not expect Argentina's actions to derail development. Navitas Petroleum Chief Executive Ian Ramsey on Tuesday welcomed Britain's support for the project. "In the face of Argentina's increasingly aggressive efforts to pressure companies associated with the development, we are grateful that the UK Government has made its position clear; that it will robustly defend the Falkland Islands' right to pursue lawful economic development," Ramsey said in a statement to Reuters.

item.title: Dólar cae desde máximo de 18 meses, mercado aguarda datos de inflación
item.description: El dólar retrocedía el martes desde sus máximos de 18 meses en línea con la caída del petróleo, mientras los inversionistas reevaluaban el repunte impulsado por la IA que ha respaldado la demanda de activos estadounidenses este año, a la espera de nuevas pistas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo, Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: El dólar retrocedía el martes desde sus máximos de 18 meses en línea con la caída del petróleo, mientras los inversionistas reevaluaban el repunte impulsado por la IA que ha respaldado la demanda de activos estadounidenses este año, a la espera de nuevas pistas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés. Los mercados esperan que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, evite una escalada en Oriente Medio y Ucrania, ya que un conflicto más amplio podría perjudicar su posición de cara a las elecciones de mitad de legislatura. Los precios del petróleo caían el martes y se encaminaban hacia su primer descenso en casi una semana mientras los operadores sopesaban la posibilidad de un aumento del suministro de gasóleo procedente de Rusia. "El dólar se muestra un poco más débil ante un ligero descenso del petróleo. Los resultados de los grandes bancos de esta mañana han sido dispares, lo que arroja poca luz sobre las perspectivas generales de la renta variable", señaló John Velis, estratega macroeconómico para América de BNY. Más allá del sector energético, algunos analistas señalaron que el reciente repunte del dólar también se ve amenazado por las crecientes dudas sobre el potencial de inversión impulsado por la inteligencia artificial. El índice dólar caía 0,25% a 102,27 unidades tras tocar el lunes las 102,61 puntos, nivel más alto desde abril de 2025. Los datos del índice de precios al consumo de septiembre, que se publicarán el miércoles, deberían aportar más pistas sobre un posible endurecimiento de la política monetaria por parte de la Fed. Los operadores estiman que hay un 80% de probabilidades de que la Fed mantenga las tasas este mes mientras que descuentan un endurecimiento de unos 75 puntos básicos para finales de 2027, según FedWatch de CME. El euro se recuperaba de un mínimo de unos 17 meses a pesar de otra alza de los precios del gas, un factor clave de la inflación en la zona del euro, mientras persistían las preocupaciones sobre las perspectivas fiscales de Francia. Subía 0,3% hasta 1,1189 dólares tras tocar el lunes los 1,11525 dólares, su nivel más bajo desde mayo de 2025. Los precios del gas natural alcanzaron los 86,71 euros, su nivel más alto desde diciembre de 2022. El yen se apreciaba un 0,15% a 158,38 unidades frente al dólar, después de que los datos del Banco de Japón mostraran que los precios al por mayor subieron un 6,8% en el año hasta septiembre. Aunque la cifra quedó por debajo de la previsión mediana del mercado de 7,6%, fue suficiente para justificar los temores del mercado a tipos de interés más altos.

item.title: Iran and Russia are stepping up hybrid campaigns in Britain, UK spy chief says
item.description: Iran is stepping up attempts to hit harder targets such as military sites in Britain and Russia is increasing its hybrid warfare against Ukraine's allies, the UK's domestic spy chief said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Michael Holden
item.content:encoded: Iran is stepping up attempts to hit harder targets such as military sites in Britain and Russia is increasing its hybrid warfare against Ukraine's allies, the UK's domestic spy chief said on Tuesday. In his annual speech on wide-ranging threats to Britain, MI5 Director General Ken McCallum also said the greatest concern about the misuse of AI was terrorists being able to develop bioweapons or even create new pathogens. McCallum said state threats had quadrupled over the last decade, and his organisation now devoted more resources to the issue than during the Cold War. On Monday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Tehran was [USN:L8N45Y178 TEXT:""highly likely""] behind a suspected plot against [USN:L1N45R08W TEXT:"RAF Fairford"], an airbase used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran. It prompted a [USN:L1N45R04X TEXT:"security alert"] and led to US President Trump withdrawing planes from the air base. Tehran has rejected accusations of involvement in the Fairford incident or any other accusations of malign activity in Britain where the authorities have for a number of years accused it of being involved in plots and attempted assassinations against dissidents and Israeli and Jewish targets. Russia also denies involvement in hostile acts in Britain and other Western countries, but McCallum said it remained the "aggressor number one". MORE THAN 50 ARRESTS LINKED TO IRAN, MCCALLUM SAYS McCallum said he could not speak about the Fairford incident because of an ongoing investigation, but he said there had been a major shift this year in "Iranian ambitions to come at harder targets, like military sites". "The RAF Fairford incident ... is not unique. There have been other examples, not just in the UK but around the world," he said. McCallum said over the past year Iran-linked operations had led to more than 50 arrests. Asked if Iran had the capability to launch complex attacks perhaps using explosive drones, McCallum said it was limited by the sophistication of the criminals and proxies it used for operations in Britain. "Given what we've actually seen in practice in the UK in recent years, that has not been anywhere near (that) level of capability," he said. "That said, clearly it is the case that in countries closer to its own homeland, the IRGC (Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps) has quite deep experience of using more conventional and hybrid technology in a more aggressive and sophisticated way." AI 'SUPERCHARGING' THREAT McCallum echoed comments from other [USN:L8N45Y0Q0 TEXT:"European spy agencies"] that [USN:L8N44U0IR TEXT:"Russia was using tactics"] just short of conventional conflict, citing the [USN:L8N44T1P2 TEXT:"attempted drone attack"] on a cargo plane at a German airport and a cyber attack on Polish energy infrastructure. "It's no accident that Russian aggressors are trying to unsettle other European homelands at a time when their military progress in Ukraine is minimal and horrifically costly." Russia has rejected Germany's accusations over the incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport in August as "entirely fabricated". Speaking about AI, McCallum said the technology was "supercharging the cybersecurity contest between attackers and defenders" and terrorists were exploiting it to improve reconnaissance and attack methodologies. "Not yet realised - the misuse case to which I'd attach greatest weight - is AI's potential to change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons," he said, adding it was the area on which he and his colleagues were "particularly focused". "These risks are real."

item.title: LSEG in talks to buy Permira-owned Octus data group for about $3.5 billion
item.description: The London Stock Exchange Group confirmed on Tuesday it is in talks with private equity firm Permira to acquire financial data group Octus for about $3.5 billion.
item.dc:creator: Amy-Jo Crowley
item.content:encoded: The London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG.L) confirmed on Tuesday it is in talks with private equity firm Permira to acquire financial data group [USN:L8N3W10ML TEXT:"Octus"] for about $3.5 billion. No final agreement has been reached and no transaction is guaranteed, LSEG said, adding that New York-headquartered Octus has a strong track record of double-digit revenue growth based on a high-retention subscription model. LSEG shares, which fell more than 2% on a Reuters [USN:L6N45R0P5 TEXT:"report"] on the talks earlier on Tuesday, extended losses to 4.7% at 1342 GMT. London-listed LSEG had a market value of $55.8 billion as of Monday's market close. "Octus' coverage and solutions are highly complementary to LSEG's existing fixed income data & analytics and private markets solutions," said exchange operator LSEG. LSEG said a takeover of Octus, which was launched by its CEO Kent Collier in 2013, would be immediately accretive to its Data & Analytics and group revenue growth. Reuters has reported that Collier still holds a minority stake in Octus, which employs journalists, analysts and legal experts to provide information on credit markets, with a focus on companies in financial distress, for banks and investors. PERMIRA BOUGHT CONTROLLING STAKE IN OCTUS IN 2022 London-based Permira is working with advisers to evaluate interest in Octus, two people with knowledge of the situation said before LSEG confirmed the talks. The private equity group, which declined to comment, has been planning a sale of Octus since last year and has also held talks with other potential buyers, one of the people said. Permira acquired a controlling stake in Octus from Warburg Pincus in 2022 at a valuation of $1.3 billion. Octus is expected to generate about $145 million of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) this year, with that figure forecast to rise to roughly $200 million next year, one of the people said. LSEG has been under pressure from activist investor Elliott Management, which [USN:L4N3Z70FN TEXT:"disclosed"] a stake in the group in February. The strategic rationale for LSEG would likely include adding proprietary and private-market data assets, creating cross-selling opportunities with Tradeweb and Yield Book, traders at one bank said, as well as expanding its client base to include private-market general partners. Similar data transactions have generally been valued at about 12 to 14 times enterprise value-to-sales, and a deal at these multiples would likely be dilutive to earnings per share. LSEG declined to comment on these observations. LSEG is the largest customer of Reuters, which provides news for its Workspace news and data platform and other products. An Octus takeover, if it goes ahead, would also mark a further uptick in [USN:L6N45K0KD TEXT:"dealmaking"] in the data analytics sector, despite a selloff in listed stocks earlier this year. YipitData, backed by investors including Carlyle Group, is exploring a sale that could value the data analytics provider at more than $2.5 billion, while Vista Equity Partners is exploring a sale of private markets data provider Allvue.

item.title: Goolsbee, de la Fed, dice que inflación causada por la IA se está "saliendo de su carril"
item.description: El presidente del Banco de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, dijo el martes que la inflación está empezando a parecer un "sobrecalentamiento agregado", impulsado por los efectos indirectos del auge de la inversión en inteligencia artificial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente del Banco de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, Austan Goolsbee, dijo el martes que la inflación está empezando a parecer un "sobrecalentamiento agregado", impulsado por los efectos indirectos del auge de la inversión en inteligencia artificial. "Esto empieza a parecer un sobrecalentamiento agregado", declaró Goolsbee a Semafor en una entrevista. "Los aumentos de los costos de los centros de datos de IA se están saliendo de su carril y los precios están subiendo en sectores que no se limitan a los componentes de los centros de datos ni a las industrias directamente relacionadas con ellos", señaló. "Si se empieza a observar que esto se extiende cada vez más a los servicios generales, que los bienes de inversión están impulsando el crecimiento del PIB a un ritmo superior al potencial y generando este tipo de inflación derivada, eso resulta problemático", indicó. "A diferencia de las perturbaciones de la oferta —de las que solemos suponer que desaparecerán por sí solas en un plazo relativamente corto—, nadie piensa lo mismo del sobrecalentamiento de la demanda", explicó. "La demanda sobrecalentada tarda mucho tiempo en ponerse en marcha y, una vez que lo hace, es difícil deshacerse de ella", señaló Goolsbee. "Por eso, la opinión generalizada entre los economistas ha sido que, si se observa un sobrecalentamiento de la demanda, hay que actuar con decisión y rapidez para evitar que eso se traduzca en expectativas de inflación y que la gente dé por sentado que nunca va a desaparecer", añadió. Cuando se le preguntó si la Fed debería seguir subiendo las tasas de interés, Goolsbee —que este año no tiene derecho a voto en materia de política monetaria—, respondió: "Si la inflación sigue siendo persistente, creo que está claro lo que tiene que hacer la Fed". "Si conseguimos alguna prueba de que esta inflación provocada por los aranceles está desapareciendo, de que la inflación derivada de la crisis del petróleo está desapareciendo, no es necesario que mostremos un gran avance", comentó. "Pero sí tenemos que empezar a mostrar algún progreso si queremos volver a la senda de recortes de tasas en la que nos encontrábamos", indicó. La Fed recortó las tasas tres veces en 2025, pero el mes pasado las subió por primera vez en tres años, al 3,75%-4%. Los mercados esperan que renuncie a otra subida en la reunión del 27 y 28 de octubre y que haya un alza efectiva de un cuarto de punto en diciembre.

item.title: Goldman Sachs beats quarterly profit estimates on equities strength
item.description: Goldman Sachs on Tuesday beat third-quarter profit estimates as dealmaking remained steady and volatile markets tied to the Middle East conflict lifted its equities revenue, sending its shares up nearly 1% in late morning trading.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Azhar, Pritam Biswas
item.content:encoded: Goldman Sachs (GS.N) on Tuesday beat third-quarter profit estimates as dealmaking remained steady and volatile markets tied to the Middle East conflict lifted its equities revenue, sending its shares up nearly 1% in late morning trading. The Wall Street giant, however, posted lower fixed income, currency and commodities revenue, in line with the third-quarter trends at rivals [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"JPMorgan Chase"] (JPM.N) and [USN:L4N45Z0VX TEXT:"Wells Fargo"] (WFC.N) . The bank's FICC business has been choppy this year. US equity markets were volatile during the quarter, driven by the Federal Reserve's interest-rate hike, rising fuel costs and a selloff in chip stocks. Investors reshuffled portfolios, resulting in higher revenue for the trading desks of banks. The equities business posted a 72% jump in quarterly revenue to $6.44 billion. "FICC came in light, which was somewhat expected based on recent bank conferences, but investment banking was a clear beat relative to consensus, which demonstrates a still robust pipeline of deal activity that is expected to keep this revenue line elevated into the next several quarters," said Stephen Biggar, analyst at Argus Research. FICC revenue came in at $3.47 billion in the third quarter, down 1% from a year ago. The business' net revenue surged 32% in the second quarter, but had dropped 10% in the first quarter when its rates business was hit by volatility from the Iran war. "Notwithstanding the current complexity and uncertainty in the world, we remain very well positioned to continue to deliver for our clients," CEO David Solomon said in a statement. Total profit was $5.29 billion, or $17.01 per share, for the three months ended September 30. That compares with $4.10 billion, or $12.25 per share, a year ago. Analysts expected a profit of $13.02 per share, according to estimates compiled by LSEG. Goldman's shares have gained about 2.7% so far in 2026, underperforming its closest peer Morgan Stanley (MS.N) and the S&P 500 (.SPX) . INVESTMENT BANKING HOLDS Goldman's investment banking division navigated a brief slowdown in dealmaking as M&A activity in the third quarter fell 41% from the prior three months to $993 billion, falling below $1 trillion for the first time since the second quarter of 2025, LSEG data showed. Investment banking fees rose 21% from a year ago to $3.22 billion. Goldman defied the broader market slowdown through higher debt and equity underwriting, alongside an 18% jump in advisory revenues. Advisory revenue was a record for the investment bank. The investment bank acted as joint lead bookrunner for Intel's (INTC.O) $23 billion equity offering and global coordinator for SK Hynix's (000660.KS) [USN:L1N43B016 TEXT:"$26.5 billion US offering"]. It also advised the New York Yankees on a $2.6 billion financing deal with Apollo Sports Capital affiliates and Nvidia (NVDA.O) on its [USN:L6N44S0PD TEXT:"$3.5 billion investment"] in MediaTek (2454.TW) . Investment banking fees dropped 5% on a sequential basis, owing to significant activity in the second quarter. "The concern would be the high-rate environment slowing IPOs planned over the next several quarters, and if investors are satisfied after repositioning putting pressure on that exceptional trading fee performance," said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management. Goldman CEO Solomon said the deals pipeline is robust despite the volatility in rates and markets. Meanwhile, rival JPMorgan (JPM.N) missed third-quarter estimates for profit on a softer performance in investment banking and less activity at its trading desks. Solomon also spoke about the opportunities and risks from the AI investment cycle that is expected to generate trillions of dollars of investments in AI-related projects over the next few years. He said it would be interesting to watch for political volatility around AI data centers ahead of midterm elections. Solomon said as the financing needs for AI projects grow and there is pressure on rates, it could affect the returns and the viability of certain projects. "But we feel very well-positioned to bring the full range of services and participate actively, and we still see an enormous amount of activity." STRESS-FREE PRIVATE CREDIT Goldman Sachs' private credit fund said in September investor requests to pull money from one of its funds slowed further in the third-quarter tender offer, keeping it under the threshold 5% cap for the third straight quarter at a time when other private credit players are facing redemption requests. The asset and wealth management division, which houses the bank's private credit fund, reported a 14% jump in its revenue, marking another strong quarter. That helped total net revenue rise 23% to its second highest at $18.68 billion. The bank has expanded its asset and wealth management business in recent years to generate steadier earnings and reduce reliance on its volatile trading and investment banking units. CEO SUCCESSION The Wall Street Journal reported last month Goldman had discussed a plan for Solomon, 64, to step down as CEO, to be replaced by Chief Operating Officer John Waldron, 57, as soon as next year, citing people familiar with the matter. "I just want to be clear: there is no succession transition or timeline underway at Goldman Sachs. The board and I are singularly focused on our strategy to grow the firm and continue to serve our clients to excel," Solomon told the analysts' briefing. "I'm really enjoying the job. But more importantly, as a team, we're super excited about what's in front of us in the coming years, and how we can continue to grow the franchise and really accelerate the earnings potential of the firm." Solomon was appointed CEO in 2018, the same year Waldron became COO. Solomon scaled back the firm's consumer banking by shedding assets after its foray into retail banking flopped.

item.title: French ministries' pension costs drain public service spending, report says
item.description: Nearly a third of some French ministries' budgets pay for the pensions of retired civil servants, squeezing out spending on other priorities such as education, a government report said, amid protests over underfunded schools.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nearly a third of some French ministries' budgets pay for the pensions of retired civil servants, squeezing out spending on other priorities such as education, a government report said, [USN:L1N45Z0DG TEXT:"amid protests"] over underfunded schools. The report, a 250-page annex to the finance bill, is the first to break down retirement costs for each ministry and comes amid growing political attention towards the cost of France's [USN:L1N45U0DV TEXT:"rising pensions bill"]. It shows that 32% of the education ministry’s budget, or €28.5 billion ($32 billion), ends up with the special pension account that funds state civil servants' pensions. "The Ministry of Finance has just dropped a real bombshell," economist Maxime Sbaihi with think tank Institut Montaigne said on X. "In the midst of a day of protest, France has learnt that a third of the budget allocated to the national education system does not actually go towards education," he added. The share for the interior ministry, which employs national police officers in France, is 30%. Across all ministries, the average is about 13%. The report, which said overall pension spending has risen by 2.5 percentage points of GDP between 2000 and 2023 while that for education has declined 0.5, follows street protests by high school students protesting poor conditions in classrooms. "The burden of pension expenditure within ministerial budgets thus has a crowding-out effect: in each ministry, the funds allocated to pensions are not available to fund public services," the report said. Pension spending is highest at the largest public employers, like the education ministry which pays teachers, because the money compensates for a demographic imbalance in the state pension scheme. The report says the state pension scheme has only 0.94 workers contributing for every pensioner, compared with 1.5 in the basic statutory private-sector scheme. Each ministry pays an employer contribution into the pension account, which has been steadily increasing as the number of retirees grows and the number of public workers shrinks. ($1 = 0.8944 euros)

item.title: Allies failed to warn Ukraine of impending missile attack, Zelenskiy says
item.description: US officials have threatened to cut off intelligence sharing and weapons sales to Ukraine unless it stops attacking Russian refineries.
item.dc:creator: Olena Harmash, Daniel Flynn
item.content:encoded: Ukraine received no prior warning from its Western partners about a Russian ballistic missile attack on its capital, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday, as Kyiv comes under intense US pressure to halt attacks on Russian refineries. Russia hit no Ukrainian energy targets overnight for the first time since US President Donald Trump's surprise Sunday announcement of an "energy ceasefire", but hammered transport and logistics with ballistic missiles and drones. Reuters and other media have reported that US officials have threatened to cut off intelligence sharing and weapons sales to Ukraine unless it stops attacking Russian refineries. Kyiv relies heavily on US intelligence for early warnings of missile strikes, experts and officials say. Zelenskiy said Ukraine had not targeted Russian refineries since Trump's announcement. However, he said Kyiv had not received the usual warning from allies of ballistic missile launches before a "particularly vile" attack on Kyiv overnight, in which five missiles hit civilian infrastructure. AIR RAID ALERTS SOUND IN KYIV ONLY AFTER BLASTS ARE HEARD "Intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches helps save lives," Zelenskiy said on X, "and this is one of the most critical issues." Air alerts sounded in Kyiv on Monday night only after several explosions had already ripped through the city. Zelenskiy stopped short of linking the lack of warning to any US threats. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha tried to calm anxiety by saying Ukraine was still receiving US military intelligence. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, he said the delay had been due to the specifics of the weaponry that Russia had used. As Ukraine fights a larger, richer and better-equipped enemy, Kyiv sees the strikes on Russian oil refineries as one of its few instruments to reduce Moscow's ability to fight. Yet Trump has repeatedly blamed Ukrainian attacks - which prompted Moscow to suspend [USN:L1N45Y0OS TEXT:"diesel exports"] - for a sharp rise in US fuel prices this year, a headache for his Republican party ahead of Congressional midterm elections in three weeks. Most analysts, however, say Trump's war in Iran has had a far greater impact on the price rise. Russia struck six Ukrainian energy sites on Monday but no strikes on energy targets were reported overnight and on Tuesday. It was unclear whether Russia had deliberately avoided targeting energy infrastructure. A Kremlin spokesman, asked about the energy ceasefire, would only say that contacts were ongoing, but declined to provide any further details. UKRAINE SAYS IT NOW HAS CARDS TO PLAY Four people were killed by Russian strikes in Ukraine's second city, Kharkiv, and dozens were injured across the country, Ukrainian officials said. The Ukrainian air force said it had not received surveillance warnings before Russia fired ballistic missiles at Kyiv late on Monday, adding that it was investigating the matter. Fabian Hoffmann, missile expert at the Norwegian Institute for Defence Studies, said Ukraine's European allies had "very limited" ability to replace US early-warning intelligence about Russian missile strikes: "Ukraine relies on the so-called Space-Based Infrared System which the US deploys - and the US system is really second to none and only the United States can provide that." Sybiha said the US request to halt attacks on Russian refineries showed how Ukraine's position had strengthened, alluding to Trump's comment to Zelenskiy in a tense Oval Office meeting last year that "you don't have the cards". "In less than two years, we have gone from 'having no cards' to 'not playing your cards'. That is an achievement," Sybiha said. Zelenskiy reiterated Ukraine's position, saying that Kyiv was ready for reciprocal steps to de-escalate, calling on partners to pressure Russia.

item.title: Wells Fargo beats profit estimates, but net interest income, revenue fall short
item.description: Wells Fargo beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit on Tuesday, but lower-than-expected net interest income and revenue sent the fourth-largest US lender's shares lower.
item.dc:creator: Utkarsh Shetti, Nivedita Balu
item.content:encoded: Wells Fargo (WFC.N) beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit on Tuesday, but lower-than-expected net interest income and revenue sent the fourth-largest US lender's shares lower. Big bank earnings have started off mixed after a volatile quarter, roiled by the conflict in Iran, higher oil prices and a global bond-market selloff. JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"fell short"] of quarterly profit estimates for the first time in nearly three years while other large institutions saw choppy activity in their fixed income, currency and commodities divisions. Wells Fargo's earnings beat was driven by robust growth in loans, but net interest income — the difference between what a lender earns on loans and pays out on deposits — fell short of expectations. That metric was hurt by lower interest rates on floating-rate assets, higher deposit costs and a decline in non interest-bearing deposits. Executives said businesses were pressured by the more challenging market environment that emerged in the last few weeks of September and the sharp move upward in interest rates. "Inflation and higher interest rates continue to be headwinds, and the longer they persist, the more pressure they can place on both consumers and commercial clients," CEO Charlie Scharf told analysts. "While markets have been strong, an unexpected or significant movement could filter through the broader economy." The bank reported a profit of $1.87 per share, beating analysts' average expectations of $1.85, according to data compiled by LSEG. Net interest income rose 5% to $12.52 billion, short of expectations of $12.63 billion. Revenue came in at $21.87 billion, short of estimates for $22.31 billion. Shares were last down about 1.3%. MARKETS PRESSURE CFO Mike Santomassimo said he expects fourth-quarter net interest income to grow, boosted by loan and deposit growth, while also benefiting from higher interest rates. However, some of those gains could be offset by the markets business, where higher borrowing costs are a drag on net interest income. That unit, which provides financing and risk management services to institutional investors, was hurt by slowed fixed income, currencies, and commodities trading. Revenue was down 1% year-over-year and off 17% from the previous quarter. Investment banking activity across Wall Street was more subdued due to market uncertainty and the surge in higher borrowing costs that spurred companies to take a wait-and-see approach to fundraising and investment. Wells has invested heavily in its investment banking and markets businesses, hiring senior bankers and spending more on client financing, trading and other capital-markets activities. Wells Fargo raked in investment banking revenue of $611 million in the quarter, up 10% from a year earlier. However, it was down 3% sequentially, mirroring a trend across peers. CONSUMER SPENDING RESILIENT Wells, which relies on consumer banking and lending for nearly half of its income, has leaned on credit cards and auto loans to grow its consumer loan book, where spending trends are healthier due to the resilience in the US economy. Average consumer loan balances grew 4% to about $342 billion, while commercial banking loans climbed 10% to $240.5 billion. "We're not seeing any change in behavior across either borrowers or depositors that would lead us to believe something's changing in the underlying trends that we've seen now," Santomassimo told reporters on a post-earnings call.
